label: Doc-version drift reduces to one segment: X.Y inherit the skill anchor (git-free, filesystem-resolved), Z is seeded 0, and only W = min(realEditCount, 99) is git-derived.

Stored W cannot stay green by workflow: writing the version is itself a numstat-counted edit, one apply pass never converges, and the only convergent flow is apply/commit/apply/amend; the count reads committed history only, so a dirty tree can verify green and go stale on the saving commit.

What can never fail today is the gate only: gate is git-free presence+format; verify compares the full tuple against git-derived values and fleet-wide mismatches are documented as expected; iterations 2-4 closed the enforcement inventory (presence/format or fixtures only; verify uncalled).

Q3 answer: the smallest green-by-construction contract is presence+format, extended by git-free era parity (child X.Y equals the owning skill anchor X.Y) with W demoted out of the stored assertion; every component is computed from the working tree, the existing post-edit gate is the only enforced surface, and the change is a deletion rather than new machinery.

External-author reading (partial): W is unreproducible outside this repository git history; the externally reproducible component is the skill-era X.Y; no in-repo definition of the term "external author" exists.
A stored invariant must be a pure function of the working tree; a git-history-derived component such as W cannot be asserted without drift.
The post-edit gate is git-free and cannot be made stale by a commit; verify is descriptive and unsuitable as a contract surface.

direction: Stored git-derived W with a better reconciliation workflow
reason: Any numstat-affecting commit stales the stored value by definition; the two-pass amend flow amortizes but never removes the per-commit ceremony.
